root_cause.text: The use of `skb_end_offset` to distinguish whether an skb head was allocated from the dedicated `skb_small_head_cache` or generic `kmalloc` is unreliable when KFENCE is enabled because `kfence_ksize()` returns the exact requested allocation size, potentially making a `kzalloc`-ed head appear to have been allocated from the small head cache, leading to a cross-cache free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "when KFENCE is enabled, kfence_ksize() returns the exact requested allocation size instead of the slab bucket size... skb_end_offset ends up matching SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM, causing skb_kfree_head() to incorrectly free the object to skb_small_head_cache." The patch removes the conditional check (`if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM) ... else kfree(head)`) and always calls `kfree(head)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unify skb head freeing by always using kfree, removing the separate small head cache path.
intent_record.what: Removed conditional branch in skb_kfree_head that differentiated between freeing from skb_small_head_cache and regular kfree, now always calls kfree.
intent_record.how: All skb heads are now freed via kfree regardless of end_offset value, eliminating the special slow path for small heads allocated from a dedicated cache.

grouping_result.intent: Unify skb head freeing by always using kfree, removing the separate small head cache path.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the separate small head cache path by unifying skb head freeing to always use kfree, which directly eliminates the unreliable distinction at the root of the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This condition uses end_offset to decide whether the head was allocated from the skb_small_head_cache or via kmalloc. With KFENCE enabled, kfence_ksize() returns the exact requested size, so an skb head allocated with kzalloc can have an end_offset equal to SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM, causing a cross-cache free when it is passed to kmem_cache_free instead of kfree.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition uses end_offset to decide whether the skb head was allocated from the dedicated small head cache. When KFENCE is enabled, kfence_ksize() returns the exact requested size, so a kzalloc-allocated head can have an end_offset equal to SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM, causing a cross-cache free if kmem_cache_free is used instead of kfree.
